resources.string: Signed and encrypted mail, and your keys
Off by default. When on, a mail that is signed or encrypted shows a status, and the whole message is fetched to check it.
Nothing is checked while this is off, and no mail is looked at for it.
Mail that is encrypted, by its sender or by the server for storage, cannot be searched by its text on the server.
No private key yet. Import one to read mail that is encrypted for you.
An armored OpenPGP key file, or a PKCS#12 file (.p12, .pfx)
None yet. Keys are only added when you choose to: from a file, from a message, or by pasting.
Import a public key or certificate
The private part is deleted from this phone. Mail that is encrypted for this key can no longer be opened here unless you import it again.
Signatures made with it can no longer be checked here until you add it again.
Remove all keys and switch off
All keys and certificates, yours with their private parts, are deleted from this phone, and the feature is switched off.
The file could not be added: %1$s
The keys could not be loaded.
The passphrase is stored in the phone\'s protected storage, so mail opens without asking. Anyone who can unlock this phone can then read mail encrypted for this key.
The key %1$s is protected by a passphrase. It is used for this message only unless you keep it unlocked.
This file is protected by a passphrase. It is only used to read the key now.
That passphrase does not open the key.
Signed, but with a different key than before
Encrypted, no key to open it
The message says it is from %1$s.
This key is in your keyring.
This key came with the message and is not in your keyring.
The check covers the whole message.
The check covers only one part of the message. Anything outside that part is not covered, whatever it looks like.

The signature is valid, nothing was changed after signing, and the address of the key is the address the message is from. Keep in mind that you added this key yourself: the check is only as good as that.
The signature is valid, but the key is not the one this sender used first. It may be a new key of the same person, or someone else. Check with the sender in another way before you rely on it.

The signature is valid, and the certificate names the address the message is from. But the certificate came with the message and is not checked against an authority, so anyone could have made it. To rely on it, add it to your keys only if you know it is right.
The signature is valid, but the key belongs to a different address than the one the message is from. Do not take the message to be from its sender.
The message is signed, but you have no key or certificate for the signer, so nothing can be said about it.
The signature does not fit the message. It was changed after it was signed, or the signature is false. Do not trust it.
The signature is valid, but the key had run out when it was used.
The signature is valid, but the key was revoked by its owner, usually because it is no longer safe.
The message is signed in a way this app cannot check: %1$s
The signature data could not be read.
The message was encrypted for you and has been opened here. It is shown on its own and is not stored on this phone.
The message is encrypted, but none of your private keys is one it was made for. Import the key to open it.
The message is encrypted for a key of yours that is protected by a passphrase.
That passphrase does not open the key.
The message is encrypted in an old way that cannot tell whether it was changed on the way, which attackers can use to read it. It is not opened.
The message is encrypted in a way this app cannot open: %1$s
The encrypted data is damaged or could not be read.
Pictures and other content from the internet stay blocked in this message, whatever you chose. Content like that can be used to read encrypted mail.
Text around the signed part was left out because the signature does not cover it.
The message was signed inside the encryption.
Encrypted mail cannot be searched by its text on the server.
For S/MIME no chain of trust and no revocation list is checked.
A key came with this message
The key could not be added.
The file could not be opened.
Opened from memory and removed again when you leave; nothing of it is kept.
